verses.1: After these events, the kings of Egypt sinned, and they became rulers over their own people as kings of Egypt.
verses.2: And Pharaoh became angry because of his two officers, the officer in charge of the grain and the officer in charge of the livestock.
verses.3: And he gave them into the custody of the house of the priests, in a place where Asur was kept.
verses.4: And the chief priests took Joseph along with them. They mistreated him, and days of suffering awaited him.
verses.5: And they both dreamed the same dream. Each of them dreamed it in one night. It was a dream about a king of Egypt, who was forbidden to enter the Temple of Set.
verses.6: And Joseph came to them in the morning. He saw them, and they were crying.
verses.7: And he asked the servers of Pharaoh, who were with him in the court of his palace, “Do you know that your faces are evil today?”
verses.8: And they said to him, “We have dreamed a dream, but there’s no solution to it.” He replied, “Tell me about these problems that you’ve encountered. Please tell me.”
verses.9: And the singer told Joseph his dream. In his dream, he saw a fig tree before him.
verses.10: And in the garden, there were three branches. It was like a flower that bloomed beautifully. Its buds turned into ripe grapes.
verses.11: And I will take the grapes from Pharaoh’s basket, and I will crush them. Then I will put the baskets on Pharaoh’s feet.
verses.12: And Joseph said to him, “This is our solution: three days of fasting.”
verses.13: In three days, Pharaoh will take your head and put you back on your feet. He will give you a chest full of treasures, as punishment for the first sin you committed.
verses.14: For if you remember me as being beneficial to you, then please show me kindness and remember me before Pharaoh. Then I will be able to get out of this house.
verses.15: For I have been stolen from the land of the Israelites. And here, I did not commit any wrongdoing, since they put me in a cage.
verses.16: And the chief priest saw that it was a good solution. He said to Joseph, “Even I am in trouble. Look, there are three bags of grain on my head.”
verses.17: And from the upper shelf, Pharaoh ate all the food that was prepared for him. He ate them from that shelf, above my head.
verses.18: And Joseph said, “This is the solution to our problem: three days.”
verses.19: In three days, Pharaoh will take your head off from you. He will hang you on a tree, and the vulture will eat your flesh from you.
verses.20: And on the third day, the day of Pharaoh’s birth, he made food for all his servants. He also placed the heads of the chefs who prepared food among his servants.
verses.21: And he placed the scepter upon its holder’s hand, and he placed the box on Pharaoh’s foot.
verses.22: And she hung up the chef’s coat, after he had finished serving them.
verses.23: And the cook didn’t remember Yosef at all; he forgot about him.
